text.p: These are the leading stories in the Malawi press on Friday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- The main opposition Malawi Congress Party (MCP) strongman John Tembo, who until last week was executive chairman for the country's biggest conglomerate Press Corporation Limited, was drawing a monthly salary of 300,000 kwacha ($20,000), beating U.S. President Bill Clinton who earns $16,667 a month.

- Education secretary Sam Safuli has dismissed accusations that government has failed to live up to its promise of paying tuition and examination fees for girls in secondary schools, and blamed the confusion at the start of the school year on poor communications.

- Malawi's commercial banks have protested to the central bank claiming unfair competition from foreign banks which they say issue loans to companies without being subjected to Malawi banking regulations.
- Works Minister Abdul Pillane is at the centre of an alleged financial scam involving more than 100,000 kwacha ($6,900).
- Stage Coach employees, the country's biggest public bus service, on Thursday went on strike over demands for improved salaries and conditions of service.
- The U.S. human rights country report says Malawi police continue to abuse detainees, enforce lengthy detentions without trial and use force to handle criminal suspects.
- Hundreds of commuters in Blantyre were stranded on Thursday due to a strike by bus operator Stage Coach employees demanding higher wages and allowances.
